The biggest and most frustrating issue is SALARY. The hikes are unbelievably low — so low that calling them a hike almost feels like a joke. Even when someone gets a promotion, the salary increase attached to it is so minimal that it barely makes any difference. Many people feel insulted rather than rewarded.
The promotion system is equally disappointing. It does not truly recognize hard work or performance. Promotions often seem to happen by default after certain years instead of based on actual contribution. Someone who works extremely hard the entire year might not get promoted simply because their “cycle” hasn’t arrived yet, while someone else gets promoted just because they have been waiting for years.
The year-end review and rating system is another complete mess. If someone already got promoted recently, they will automatically be given a default “succeeding” rating regardless of how exceptional their work was and that makes their “peanut” hikes become almost invisible. Meanwhile, someone who hasn’t been promoted for years might suddenly receive higher ratings just because it’s their turn. This makes the entire performance evaluation system feel unfair and meaningless.
The most painful part is when you give your full effort, work late hours,solve difficult problems, and genuinely care about your work, only to end up with the same rating as someone who barely worked all year. That completely destroys motivation. 
Because of these issues — pathetic salary hikes, delayed promotions, and a broken rating system — many talented and hardworking employees are leaving the company.The company is slowly losing good people because they simply feel undervalued.
No meaningful hikes, almost no onsite opportunities, and limited career growth.
At the same time, strict policies like hybrid work enforcement are pushed without giving employees proper flexibility for work from home.
Many employees are staying only because of circumstances — not because they believe in the company anymore.
Honestly, it feels like hard work is not rewarded here, and the system is designed to discourage the very people who try the hardest.

benefits.name: Pension
benefits.details: Every employee has a pension plan with us. We have our own pension fund for this, specifically the Stichting Pensioenfonds Capgemini Nederland. The pension plan is non-contributory, which means you do not have to pay anything into it. But if you want to contribute and supplement your pension, you can use the voluntary pension plan.

benefits.name: Mobility
benefits.details: As a consultant, you frequently work for different clients throughout the country. That is why every employee of ours receives a mobility allowance. How you spend this mobility allowance is up to you. You can opt for a leased car, a kilometer allowance for using your own car, or an NS Business Card. Or you could opt to have the amount paid out gross.

benefits.name: Leave
benefits.details: Will you be working full time? Then per calendar year, you will be entitled to 20 statutory days off and 6 days in excess of the legal requirement. We also pay out a vacation allowance once a year. Besides this, you have all the national public holidays off, of course, and Capgemini also provides special paid leave, maternity leave, and parental leave.

benefits.name: Flexible working
benefits.details: Need to drop your children off at school before coming to the office? Or want to start early so that you have time for sports after work? At Capgemini, you are free to decide where and when you work. The laptop, SIM card, and connectivity allowance you receive allow you to log in from anywhere. Of course, it is a good idea to discuss your work times and location with the client for whom you are working.

benefits.name: Salary
benefits.details: We use salary grades at Capgemini. A grade indicates the degree of seniority at Capgemini and serves as the basis for determining your salary. If you join us, you will be assigned to one of our six grades at the start of your career. This depends on your knowledge and experience, of course. A grade is not related to your place in the organization. This means that you genuinely receive recognition for your individual development, knowledge, experience, and level. And not for your position in the hierarchical line.

questions.question: what is POM.xml, what is .m2 , what is difference between Sanpshot and release in Maven
questions.answer: POM.xml is a Maven project configuration file, .m2 is the local repository, and SNAPSHOTs are development versions while releases are stable.POM.xml (Project Object Model) defines project structure, dependencies, and build configurations in Maven.Example of POM.xml: <project><modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion><groupId>com.example</groupId><artifactId>my-app</artifactId><version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version></project>.m2 is the local repository where Maven stores downloaded dependencies and project artifacts.SNAPSHOT versions (e.g., 1.0-SNAPSHOT) are for ongoing development and can change, while release versions (e.g., 1.0) are stable and immutable.Maven checks for updates in SNAPSHOT versions, but not for release versions.

questions.question: What is the Playwright framework and what are its key features?
questions.answer: Playwright is an open-source automation framework for web applications, enabling cross-browser testing with ease.Cross-browser support: Works with Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, allowing testing across different browsers.Auto-waiting: Automatically waits for elements to be ready before performing actions, reducing flakiness in tests.Headless mode: Supports running tests in headless mode, which speeds up execution and is useful for CI/CD pipelines.Powerful API: Provides a rich set of APIs for interacting with web elements, such as click, fill, and navigate.Network interception: Allows testing of network requests and responses, enabling validation of API interactions.

questions.question: What are the methods for taking screenshots and recording video?
questions.answer: Screenshots and video recording can be achieved using various tools and methods in automation testing.Using built-in methods in automation frameworks like Selenium: `driver.get_screenshot_as_file('screenshot.png')`.Utilizing third-party libraries such as AShot for screenshots: `new AShot().shootingStrategy(new ViewportPastingStrategy(1000)).takeScreenshot(driver).getImage()`.For video recording, tools like FFmpeg can be used to capture screen activity during test execution.Using screen recording software like OBS Studio or Camtasia to manually record test sessions.In mobile testing, tools like Appium provide methods to capture screenshots and record videos of app interactions.

questions.question: What are assertions do you have used?
questions.answer: Assertions are crucial in automation testing to validate expected outcomes against actual results.AssertEquals: Validates if two values are equal. Example: assertEquals(expectedValue, actualValue);AssertTrue: Checks if a condition is true. Example: assertTrue(isConditionMet);AssertFalse: Checks if a condition is false. Example: assertFalse(isConditionNotMet);AssertNotNull: Ensures an object is not null. Example: assertNotNull(object);AssertSame: Validates if two references point to the same object. Example: assertSame(expectedObject, actualObject);

questions.question: Explain background keyword
questions.answer: The background keyword in automation testing allows tests to run in parallel without blocking the main execution flow.Enables concurrent execution of tests, improving efficiency.Example: Running multiple test cases simultaneously to save time.Helps in scenarios where tests are independent and can run in isolation.Useful in CI/CD pipelines to ensure faster feedback loops.

questions.question: Explain async/await
questions.answer: Async/await simplifies asynchronous programming in JavaScript, making it easier to read and write code that handles promises.Async functions return a promise, allowing for easier error handling.Await pauses the execution of the async function until the promise is resolved.Example: async function fetchData() { const data = await fetch(url); }Using async/await makes code look synchronous, improving readability.

questions.question: How can we do parallel testing
questions.answer: Parallel testing allows multiple tests to run simultaneously, improving efficiency and reducing overall testing time.Use test frameworks like TestNG or JUnit that support parallel execution.Leverage Selenium Grid to run tests on multiple machines or browsers at the same time.Implement CI/CD tools like Jenkins to automate and parallelize test execution.Utilize cloud-based testing services like BrowserStack or Sauce Labs for parallel testing across different environments.

questions.question: How do you manage test data
questions.answer: Effective test data management involves creating, maintaining, and utilizing data sets for comprehensive testing.Identify data requirements: Understand what data is needed for different test scenarios, e.g., valid, invalid, boundary cases.Data generation: Use tools like Faker or custom scripts to generate realistic test data, ensuring it mimics production data.Data masking: For sensitive information, apply data masking techniques to protect personal data while still allowing for testing.Version control: Maintain versions of test data to ensure consistency across test cycles and facilitate rollback if needed.Data cleanup: Implement processes to clean up test data after tests to avoid contamination in subsequent test runs.

questions.question: How to handle frames and network interception

questions.question: what is POM.xml, what is .m2 , what is difference between Sanpshot and release in Maven
questions.answer: POM.xml is a Maven project configuration file, .m2 is the local repository, and SNAPSHOTs are development versions while releases are stable.POM.xml (Project Object Model) defines project structure, dependencies, and build configurations in Maven.Example of POM.xml: <project><modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion><groupId>com.example</groupId><artifactId>my-app</artifactId><version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version></project>.m2 is the local repository where Maven stores downloaded dependencies and project artifacts.SNAPSHOT versions (e.g., 1.0-SNAPSHOT) are for ongoing development and can change, while release versions (e.g., 1.0) are stable and immutable.Maven checks for updates in SNAPSHOT versions, but not for release versions.

questions.question: What is the Playwright framework and what are its key features?
questions.answer: Playwright is an open-source automation framework for web applications, enabling cross-browser testing with ease.Cross-browser support: Works with Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, allowing testing across different browsers.Auto-waiting: Automatically waits for elements to be ready before performing actions, reducing flakiness in tests.Headless mode: Supports running tests in headless mode, which speeds up execution and is useful for CI/CD pipelines.Powerful API: Provides a rich set of APIs for interacting with web elements, such as click, fill, and navigate.Network interception: Allows testing of network requests and responses, enabling validation of API interactions.

questions.question: What are the methods for taking screenshots and recording video?
questions.answer: Screenshots and video recording can be achieved using various tools and methods in automation testing.Using built-in methods in automation frameworks like Selenium: `driver.get_screenshot_as_file('screenshot.png')`.Utilizing third-party libraries such as AShot for screenshots: `new AShot().shootingStrategy(new ViewportPastingStrategy(1000)).takeScreenshot(driver).getImage()`.For video recording, tools like FFmpeg can be used to capture screen activity during test execution.Using screen recording software like OBS Studio or Camtasia to manually record test sessions.In mobile testing, tools like Appium provide methods to capture screenshots and record videos of app interactions.

questions.question: What are assertions do you have used?
questions.answer: Assertions are crucial in automation testing to validate expected outcomes against actual results.AssertEquals: Validates if two values are equal. Example: assertEquals(expectedValue, actualValue);AssertTrue: Checks if a condition is true. Example: assertTrue(isConditionMet);AssertFalse: Checks if a condition is false. Example: assertFalse(isConditionNotMet);AssertNotNull: Ensures an object is not null. Example: assertNotNull(object);AssertSame: Validates if two references point to the same object. Example: assertSame(expectedObject, actualObject);

questions.question: Explain background keyword
questions.answer: The background keyword in automation testing allows tests to run in parallel without blocking the main execution flow.Enables concurrent execution of tests, improving efficiency.Example: Running multiple test cases simultaneously to save time.Helps in scenarios where tests are independent and can run in isolation.Useful in CI/CD pipelines to ensure faster feedback loops.

questions.question: Explain async/await
questions.answer: Async/await simplifies asynchronous programming in JavaScript, making it easier to read and write code that handles promises.Async functions return a promise, allowing for easier error handling.Await pauses the execution of the async function until the promise is resolved.Example: async function fetchData() { const data = await fetch(url); }Using async/await makes code look synchronous, improving readability.

questions.question: How can we do parallel testing

questions.question: How do you manage test data
questions.answer: Effective test data management involves creating, maintaining, and utilizing data sets for comprehensive testing.Identify data requirements: Understand what data is needed for different test scenarios, e.g., valid, invalid, boundary cases.Data generation: Use tools like Faker or custom scripts to generate realistic test data, ensuring it mimics production data.Data masking: For sensitive information, apply data masking techniques to protect personal data while still allowing for testing.Version control: Maintain versions of test data to ensure consistency across test cycles and facilitate rollback if needed.Data cleanup: Implement processes to clean up test data after tests to avoid contamination in subsequent test runs.

questions.question: what is POM.xml, what is .m2 , what is difference between Sanpshot and release in Maven

questions.question: What is the Playwright framework and what are its key features?
questions.answer: Playwright is an open-source automation framework for web applications, enabling cross-browser testing with ease.Cross-browser support: Works with Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, allowing testing across different browsers.Auto-waiting: Automatically waits for elements to be ready before performing actions, reducing flakiness in tests.Headless mode: Supports running tests in headless mode, which speeds up execution and is useful for CI/CD pipelines.Powerful API: Provides a rich set of APIs for interacting with web elements, such as click, fill, and navigate.Network interception: Allows testing of network requests and responses, enabling validation of API interactions.

questions.question: What are the methods for taking screenshots and recording video?
questions.answer: Screenshots and video recording can be achieved using various tools and methods in automation testing.Using built-in methods in automation frameworks like Selenium: `driver.get_screenshot_as_file('screenshot.png')`.Utilizing third-party libraries such as AShot for screenshots: `new AShot().shootingStrategy(new ViewportPastingStrategy(1000)).takeScreenshot(driver).getImage()`.For video recording, tools like FFmpeg can be used to capture screen activity during test execution.Using screen recording software like OBS Studio or Camtasia to manually record test sessions.In mobile testing, tools like Appium provide methods to capture screenshots and record videos of app interactions.

questions.question: What are assertions do you have used?

questions.question: Explain background keyword

questions.question: Explain async/await

questions.question: What are assertions do you have used?
questions.answer: Assertions are crucial in automation testing to validate expected outcomes against actual results.AssertEquals: Validates if two values are equal. Example: assertEquals(expectedValue, actualValue);AssertTrue: Checks if a condition is true. Example: assertTrue(isConditionMet);AssertFalse: Checks if a condition is false. Example: assertFalse(isConditionNotMet);AssertNotNull: Ensures an object is not null. Example: assertNotNull(object);AssertSame: Validates if two references point to the same object. Example: assertSame(expectedObject, actualObject);

questions.question: Explain background keyword
questions.answer: The background keyword in automation testing allows tests to run in parallel without blocking the main execution flow.Enables concurrent execution of tests, improving efficiency.Example: Running multiple test cases simultaneously to save time.Helps in scenarios where tests are independent and can run in isolation.Useful in CI/CD pipelines to ensure faster feedback loops.

questions.question: Explain async/await
questions.answer: Async/await simplifies asynchronous programming in JavaScript, making it easier to read and write code that handles promises.Async functions return a promise, allowing for easier error handling.Await pauses the execution of the async function until the promise is resolved.Example: async function fetchData() { const data = await fetch(url); }Using async/await makes code look synchronous, improving readability.

questions.question: How can we do parallel testing
questions.answer: Parallel testing allows multiple tests to run simultaneously, improving efficiency and reducing overall testing time.Use test frameworks like TestNG or JUnit that support parallel execution.Leverage Selenium Grid to run tests on multiple machines or browsers at the same time.Implement CI/CD tools like Jenkins to automate and parallelize test execution.Utilize cloud-based testing services like BrowserStack or Sauce Labs for parallel testing across different environments.

questions.question: How do you manage test data
questions.answer: Effective test data management involves creating, maintaining, and utilizing data sets for comprehensive testing.Identify data requirements: Understand what data is needed for different test scenarios, e.g., valid, invalid, boundary cases.Data generation: Use tools like Faker or custom scripts to generate realistic test data, ensuring it mimics production data.Data masking: For sensitive information, apply data masking techniques to protect personal data while still allowing for testing.Version control: Maintain versions of test data to ensure consistency across test cycles and facilitate rollback if needed.Data cleanup: Implement processes to clean up test data after tests to avoid contamination in subsequent test runs.

questions.question: what is POM.xml, what is .m2 , what is difference between Sanpshot and release in Maven

questions.question: what is POM.xml, what is .m2 , what is difference between Sanpshot and release in Maven
questions.answer: POM.xml is a Maven project configuration file, .m2 is the local repository, and SNAPSHOTs are development versions while releases are stable.POM.xml (Project Object Model) defines project structure, dependencies, and build configurations in Maven.Example of POM.xml: <project><modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion><groupId>com.example</groupId><artifactId>my-app</artifactId><version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version></project>.m2 is the local repository where Maven stores downloaded dependencies and project artifacts.SNAPSHOT versions (e.g., 1.0-SNAPSHOT) are for ongoing development and can change, while release versions (e.g., 1.0) are stable and immutable.Maven checks for updates in SNAPSHOT versions, but not for release versions.

questions.question: What is the Playwright framework and what are its key features?
questions.answer: Playwright is an open-source automation framework for web applications, enabling cross-browser testing with ease.Cross-browser support: Works with Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, allowing testing across different browsers.Auto-waiting: Automatically waits for elements to be ready before performing actions, reducing flakiness in tests.Headless mode: Supports running tests in headless mode, which speeds up execution and is useful for CI/CD pipelines.Powerful API: Provides a rich set of APIs for interacting with web elements, such as click, fill, and navigate.Network interception: Allows testing of network requests and responses, enabling validation of API interactions.

questions.question: What are the methods for taking screenshots and recording video?
questions.answer: Screenshots and video recording can be achieved using various tools and methods in automation testing.Using built-in methods in automation frameworks like Selenium: `driver.get_screenshot_as_file('screenshot.png')`.Utilizing third-party libraries such as AShot for screenshots: `new AShot().shootingStrategy(new ViewportPastingStrategy(1000)).takeScreenshot(driver).getImage()`.For video recording, tools like FFmpeg can be used to capture screen activity during test execution.Using screen recording software like OBS Studio or Camtasia to manually record test sessions.In mobile testing, tools like Appium provide methods to capture screenshots and record videos of app interactions.

questions.question: What are assertions do you have used?
questions.answer: Assertions are crucial in automation testing to validate expected outcomes against actual results.AssertEquals: Validates if two values are equal. Example: assertEquals(expectedValue, actualValue);AssertTrue: Checks if a condition is true. Example: assertTrue(isConditionMet);AssertFalse: Checks if a condition is false. Example: assertFalse(isConditionNotMet);AssertNotNull: Ensures an object is not null. Example: assertNotNull(object);AssertSame: Validates if two references point to the same object. Example: assertSame(expectedObject, actualObject);

questions.question: Explain background keyword
questions.answer: The background keyword in automation testing allows tests to run in parallel without blocking the main execution flow.Enables concurrent execution of tests, improving efficiency.Example: Running multiple test cases simultaneously to save time.Helps in scenarios where tests are independent and can run in isolation.Useful in CI/CD pipelines to ensure faster feedback loops.

questions.question: Explain async/await
questions.answer: Async/await simplifies asynchronous programming in JavaScript, making it easier to read and write code that handles promises.Async functions return a promise, allowing for easier error handling.Await pauses the execution of the async function until the promise is resolved.Example: async function fetchData() { const data = await fetch(url); }Using async/await makes code look synchronous, improving readability.

questions.question: How can we do parallel testing
questions.answer: Parallel testing allows multiple tests to run simultaneously, improving efficiency and reducing overall testing time.Use test frameworks like TestNG or JUnit that support parallel execution.Leverage Selenium Grid to run tests on multiple machines or browsers at the same time.Implement CI/CD tools like Jenkins to automate and parallelize test execution.Utilize cloud-based testing services like BrowserStack or Sauce Labs for parallel testing across different environments.

questions.question: How do you manage test data
questions.answer: Effective test data management involves creating, maintaining, and utilizing data sets for comprehensive testing.Identify data requirements: Understand what data is needed for different test scenarios, e.g., valid, invalid, boundary cases.Data generation: Use tools like Faker or custom scripts to generate realistic test data, ensuring it mimics production data.Data masking: For sensitive information, apply data masking techniques to protect personal data while still allowing for testing.Version control: Maintain versions of test data to ensure consistency across test cycles and facilitate rollback if needed.Data cleanup: Implement processes to clean up test data after tests to avoid contamination in subsequent test runs.

questions.question: what is POM.xml, what is .m2 , what is difference between Sanpshot and release in Maven
questions.answer: POM.xml is a Maven project configuration file, .m2 is the local repository, and SNAPSHOTs are development versions while releases are stable.POM.xml (Project Object Model) defines project structure, dependencies, and build configurations in Maven.Example of POM.xml: <project><modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion><groupId>com.example</groupId><artifactId>my-app</artifactId><version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version></project>.m2 is the local repository where Maven stores downloaded dependencies and project artifacts.SNAPSHOT versions (e.g., 1.0-SNAPSHOT) are for ongoing development and can change, while release versions (e.g., 1.0) are stable and immutable.Maven checks for updates in SNAPSHOT versions, but not for release versions.

questions.question: What is the Playwright framework and what are its key features?
questions.answer: Playwright is an open-source automation framework for web applications, enabling cross-browser testing with ease.Cross-browser support: Works with Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, allowing testing across different browsers.Auto-waiting: Automatically waits for elements to be ready before performing actions, reducing flakiness in tests.Headless mode: Supports running tests in headless mode, which speeds up execution and is useful for CI/CD pipelines.Powerful API: Provides a rich set of APIs for interacting with web elements, such as click, fill, and navigate.Network interception: Allows testing of network requests and responses, enabling validation of API interactions.

questions.question: What are the methods for taking screenshots and recording video?
questions.answer: Screenshots and video recording can be achieved using various tools and methods in automation testing.Using built-in methods in automation frameworks like Selenium: `driver.get_screenshot_as_file('screenshot.png')`.Utilizing third-party libraries such as AShot for screenshots: `new AShot().shootingStrategy(new ViewportPastingStrategy(1000)).takeScreenshot(driver).getImage()`.For video recording, tools like FFmpeg can be used to capture screen activity during test execution.Using screen recording software like OBS Studio or Camtasia to manually record test sessions.In mobile testing, tools like Appium provide methods to capture screenshots and record videos of app interactions.

questions.question: What are assertions do you have used?
questions.answer: Assertions are crucial in automation testing to validate expected outcomes against actual results.AssertEquals: Validates if two values are equal. Example: assertEquals(expectedValue, actualValue);AssertTrue: Checks if a condition is true. Example: assertTrue(isConditionMet);AssertFalse: Checks if a condition is false. Example: assertFalse(isConditionNotMet);AssertNotNull: Ensures an object is not null. Example: assertNotNull(object);AssertSame: Validates if two references point to the same object. Example: assertSame(expectedObject, actualObject);

questions.question: Explain background keyword
questions.answer: The background keyword in automation testing allows tests to run in parallel without blocking the main execution flow.Enables concurrent execution of tests, improving efficiency.Example: Running multiple test cases simultaneously to save time.Helps in scenarios where tests are independent and can run in isolation.Useful in CI/CD pipelines to ensure faster feedback loops.

questions.question: Explain async/await
questions.answer: Async/await simplifies asynchronous programming in JavaScript, making it easier to read and write code that handles promises.Async functions return a promise, allowing for easier error handling.Await pauses the execution of the async function until the promise is resolved.Example: async function fetchData() { const data = await fetch(url); }Using async/await makes code look synchronous, improving readability.

questions.question: How can we do parallel testing

questions.question: How do you manage test data
questions.answer: Effective test data management involves creating, maintaining, and utilizing data sets for comprehensive testing.Identify data requirements: Understand what data is needed for different test scenarios, e.g., valid, invalid, boundary cases.Data generation: Use tools like Faker or custom scripts to generate realistic test data, ensuring it mimics production data.Data masking: For sensitive information, apply data masking techniques to protect personal data while still allowing for testing.Version control: Maintain versions of test data to ensure consistency across test cycles and facilitate rollback if needed.Data cleanup: Implement processes to clean up test data after tests to avoid contamination in subsequent test runs.

questions.answer: Playwright is an open-source automation framework for web applications, enabling cross-browser testing with ease.Cross-browser support: Works with Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, allowing testing across different browsers.Auto-waiting: Automatically waits for elements to be ready before performing actions, reducing flakiness in tests.Headless mode: Supports running tests in headless mode, which speeds up execution and is useful for CI/CD pipelines.Powerful API: Provides a rich set of APIs for interacting with web elements, such as click, fill, and navigate.Network interception: Allows testing of network requests and responses, enabling validation of API interactions.

questions.question: What are the methods for taking screenshots and recording video?
questions.answer: Screenshots and video recording can be achieved using various tools and methods in automation testing.Using built-in methods in automation frameworks like Selenium: `driver.get_screenshot_as_file('screenshot.png')`.Utilizing third-party libraries such as AShot for screenshots: `new AShot().shootingStrategy(new ViewportPastingStrategy(1000)).takeScreenshot(driver).getImage()`.For video recording, tools like FFmpeg can be used to capture screen activity during test execution.Using screen recording software like OBS Studio or Camtasia to manually record test sessions.In mobile testing, tools like Appium provide methods to capture screenshots and record videos of app interactions.

questions.question: What are assertions do you have used?
questions.answer: Assertions are crucial in automation testing to validate expected outcomes against actual results.AssertEquals: Validates if two values are equal. Example: assertEquals(expectedValue, actualValue);AssertTrue: Checks if a condition is true. Example: assertTrue(isConditionMet);AssertFalse: Checks if a condition is false. questions.question: Explain background keyword
questions.answer: The background keyword in automation testing allows tests to run in parallel without blocking the main execution flow.Enables concurrent execution of tests, improving efficiency.Example: Running multiple test cases simultaneously to save time.Helps in scenarios where tests are independent and can run in isolation.Useful in CI/CD pipelines to ensure faster feedback loops.

questions.question: Explain async/await
questions.answer: Async/await simplifies asynchronous programming in JavaScript, making it easier to read and write code that handles promises.Async functions return a promise, allowing for easier error handling.Await pauses the execution of the async function until the promise is resolved.Example: async function fetchData() { const data = await fetch(url); }Using async/await makes code look synchronous, improving readability.

questions.question: How do you manage test data

questions.question: Swapping of 2 numbers without 3rd variable, iterate a list using Iterator
questions.answer: Swapping two numbers without a third variable can be done using arithmetic operations or bitwise XOR.Use addition and subtraction: a = a + b; b = a - b; a = a - b.Use multiplication and division: a = a * b; b = a / b; a = a / b (ensure b != 0).Use bitwise XOR: a = a ^ b; b = a ^ b; a = a ^ b.Iterate a list using Iterator in Java: List<Integer> list = Arrays.asList(1, 2, 3); Iterator<Integer> it = list.iterator(); while(it.hasNext()) { System.out.println(it.next()); }

questions.question: what is POM.xml, what is .m2 , what is difference between Sanpshot and release in Maven
questions.answer: POM.xml is a Maven project configuration file, .m2 is the local repository, and SNAPSHOTs are development versions while releases are stable.POM.xml (Project Object Model) defines project structure, dependencies, and build configurations in Maven.Example of POM.xml: <project><modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion><groupId>com.example</groupId><artifactId>my-app</artifactId><version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version></project>.m2 is the local repository where Maven stores downloaded dependencies and project artifacts.SNAPSHOT versions (e.g., 1.0-SNAPSHOT) are for ongoing development and can change, while release versions (e.g., 1.0) are stable and immutable.Maven checks for updates in SNAPSHOT versions, but not for release versions.
